purpose: A versioned pairing envelope carrying ONLY safe, temporary information: enough for the phone to reach the Tower through the network context it is actually in, without ever carrying a durable credential. Defines the QR payload contract the Tower emits (v3) and the Android client consumes; v2 remains parseable (compatibility matrix below).
design_rules: R-ENVELOPE-1: the QR carries a signed, short-lived (120-300 s) envelope; nothing durable
R-ENVELOPE-2: every field is either public (ids, endpoints) or a REFERENCE (nonce_ref, phrase REFERENCE — never the phrase itself)
R-ENVELOPE-3: forbidden-secret gate runs BEFORE any other parsing (fail closed, inherited from v2)
R-ENVELOPE-4: at least one endpoint candidate SHOULD be reachable from a cellular context for the envelope to be universally usable; the Tower SHOULD emit every physically-available class

R-ENVELOPE-5: no endpoint is ever hardcoded in the Android source; the ONLY endpoint sources are the envelope, Owner-configured alternates (manual advanced), LAN discovery (NSD), and MagicDNS names entered/guided by the Owner

v.note: envelope schema version; v2 payloads remain accepted (single-endpoint compat)

tower_public_id.note: stable public instance identifier (was tower_instance_id in v2); safe to display

challenge_id.note: the pairing session identifier == pairings/{id} path segment (was pairing_id)

nonce_hash_or_reference.note: opaque single-use nonce REFERENCE (v2: nonce_ref); the raw nonce never travels; client replays-protection keys on this

max_claims.note: how many claim attempts the Tower allows (bounded attempts)

issued_at.note: epoch seconds; client rejects future-dated envelopes beyond clock skew tolerance (300 s)

expires_at.note: epoch seconds; TTL 120-300 s; client rejects expired before ANY network attempt

fields.note: the phrase itself is NEVER in the QR — the Tower shows it, the Owner matches it on the phone screen against the phrase_hint returned by attest (bilateral confirmation)

transport_class.note: MANUAL_ADVANCED is never IN the QR — it is a client-side Owner fallback method

url_or_host.note: https URL or bare host; LAN_MDNS carries host.local, LAN_IP carries https://192.168.x.y:port, TAILSCALE_MAGICDNS carries https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net, QUALIFIED_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT carries the CA-covered public URL

priority.note: lower = preferred; Tower orders by its own reachability expectation

tls_requirement.note: LAN_SELF_SIGNED_EXPECTED candidates are NEVER auto-trusted — they require the explicit Owner development-trust path or fail closed

expiry.note: epoch seconds; candidate-level expiry (<= envelope expires_at)

qualification_state.note: Tower-side qualification; the client re-verifies locally (freshness, TLS, reachability) and NEVER trusts the server qualification alone

public_cert_sha256.note: SHA-256 of the DER cert the public endpoint serves — pinning REFERENCE for diagnostics (comparison only, never silent trust)

public_cert_sans.note: expected SANs of the qualified public endpoint

fields.note: metadata is for VERIFICATION and DIAGNOSTICS; a mismatch is a typed TLS_HOSTNAME_MISMATCH / TLS_CA_UNTRUSTED failure, never a reason to weaken TLS

scope_request.note: minimal scopes requested, e.g. ['voice','archive:read']; displayed to the Owner before confirmation

capability_negotiation_version.note: e.g. 'capneg/1'; the post-pairing capability negotiation contract id

signature.note: unchanged from v2; the client does not verify the signature locally (the Tower proves possession at claim time); the signature makes the envelope tamper-evident for later audit

qr_text_example_shape: base64url({v:3, protocol_version:'voice-console/2', tower_public_id:'…', challenge_id:'…', nonce_hash_or_reference:'…', single_use_binding:{…}, issued_at:…, expires_at:…, verification_phrase_reference:{…}, endpoint_candidates:[…], transport_candidates:['HTTPS_POST','HTTPS_GET_POLL'], certificate_trust_metadata:{…}, scope_request:['voice','archive:read'], capability_negotiation_version:'capneg/1'}).base64url(sig)
